---
title: 'Promote builds between tracks'
status: implemented
description: 'Set up internal, beta and production tracks on an app and promote a tested Google Play or TestFlight build between them without rebuilding it.'
---

A track names where an app's releases go: a store destination, the staged
rollout for releases promoted into it, and whether a promotion needs an
approval, and from whom. A build that passed internal testing is promoted to
beta or production as the same version code, or, on the App Store, as the
same TestFlight build. Nothing is rebuilt or uploaded again, so what users
get is exactly what testers checked.

The API and the CLI call a track an **environment**
(`/environments`, `environment_id`). The web app calls it a track.

Apps without tracks keep working as before: each pipeline's
publish settings decide where its uploads go.

## What you need

- App maintainer, instance admin, or instance owner access to add
  tracks and to promote. Developers can ask for a promotion into a
  track that requires approval. Who approves is set per track;
  by default it is any maintainer.
- Google Play connected on the app's **Stores** tab. See
  [Publish to Google Play](/build/distribute/google-play). Promotion uses the
  same service account, from the daemon host.
- A first upload of the build to a Play track, such as internal testing.
- For the App Store: App Store Connect connected on the app's **Stores** tab,
  and App Store publishing to TestFlight set up on the pipeline. See
  [Publish to the App Store](/build/distribute/app-store). The build needs a
  TestFlight release that testers already have.

## 1. Add tracks

On the app, open the **Stores** tab. Under **Google Play** or **App Store
Connect**, select **Add track**. Set **Name**, **Key** and where it goes
(**Play track** on Google Play), turn on **Require approval** where someone
must sign off (see [Choose who approves](#choose-who-approves)), and set the
rollout. Select **Edit** on a track to change it in place. Add them in
promotion order, for example:

| Name       | Key          | Play track   | Approval | Rollout                           |
| ---------- | ------------ | ------------ | -------- | --------------------------------- |
| Internal   | `internal`   | `internal`   | Off      | Full release                      |
| Beta       | `beta`       | `open`       | On       | 50%, then 100% after 12 hours     |
| Production | `production` | `production` | On       | 1, 5, 20, 50, 100% every 24 hours |

The key is fixed once created; configuration files will refer to tracks by key.
Each store destination belongs to at most one track. Google Play runs staged
rollouts only on the production and open testing tracks. On internal, closed
and custom tracks a promotion is always a full release, so Oore refuses a
staged rollout policy for those tracks when you save them, instead of Play
refusing it in the middle of a promotion.

App Store Connect tracks go to one of two places (**Goes to**):

| Name       | Key          | Goes to              | Approval | Rollout                        |
| ---------- | ------------ | -------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------ |
| TestFlight | `testflight` | `Internal` (a group) | Off      | None                           |
| External   | `external`   | `External` (a group) | Off      | None                           |
| App Store  | `app-store`  | `app_store`          | On       | Phased release, or all at once |

- A **TestFlight group** is the group's name as App Store Connect shows
  it. Several groups are separated by `, `, the same way an upload records
  them. TestFlight has no staged rollout, so the rollout policy is not used.
- **App Store version** (`app_store` in the API) is the app's App Store
  version. Turn on **Phased release** to release over seven days on Apple's
  schedule (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100%); off releases to everyone once Apple
  approves the version. From the API, a rollout policy with more than one
  step turns on phased release; Oore's steps and interval do not change
  Apple's schedule. Turn on **Submit for review** (`submit_for_review`) to
  submit the version for App Review after the build is attached; otherwise it
  waits for you to submit it in App Store Connect. Submit for review is only
  available here.

From the API, use
[Create environment](/openapi/operations/create_project_environment):

```bash
curl -X POST "$OORE_URL/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/environments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OORE_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "key": "production",
    "name": "Production",
    "store": "google_play",
    "track": "production",
    "approval_required": true,
    "rollout_policy": {
      "steps": [0.01, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1],
      "interval_hours": 24,
      "crash_rate_threshold": 0.02
    }
  }'
```

A release that a pipeline uploads to a track's store destination lands in
that track, so the first upload to `internal` shows under **Internal**.
For now that upload keeps the pipeline's own rollout policy; the
track's policy applies to releases promoted into it.

Once a track has releases, where it goes is fixed. To go somewhere else, add
a new track.

## 2. Promote a build

The app's **Releases** tab lists every track with the version it has and one
next action: **Promote**, **Approve**, **Halt** or **Resume**. Other release
actions sit in the menu beside it.

1. Select **Promote** on the track that holds the build.
2. In **Promote to**, choose the target track. The list shows only
   tracks in the store the build was released to.
3. In **Reason**, say why, such as `QA signed off on 2.4.0`.
4. Select **Promote**. When the target requires approval, the button reads
   **Ask to promote** and the promotion waits for an approver.

On Google Play, the daemon assigns the release's version code to the target
track in one Play edit, keeping its release name and notes, then records a
release with the target track's rollout policy. The rollout monitor
raises it on schedule and halts it on a crash-rate breach like any other
release.

On the App Store, the daemon reuses the build Apple already processed for the
TestFlight release, with the same App Store Connect calls that upload
distribution makes:

- **TestFlight group to TestFlight group**: the build is added to the target
  groups. An external group needs TestFlight beta review first; the daemon
  submits the build unless Apple already reviewed it, and the release shows
  **In review** until Apple decides.
- **TestFlight to the App Store**: the build is attached to the app's App
  Store version with the same version string, which must be one Apple still
  lets you edit. Create the version and prepare its metadata in App Store
  Connect first. Promotion sets "What's New" to the app version's release
  notes when it has some; otherwise App Store Connect keeps what it has. The
  promote dialog shows the notes, with **Edit**. Phased release is turned on or off from the track,
  and the version is submitted for review when the track says so. The
  release shows **In review**, then follows App Review and phased release in
  App Store Connect.

Promotions into the App Store version are serialised per track, and
only one build at a time can hold the version: while another build's release
is in review or releasing on it, a second build is refused.

```bash
curl -X POST "$OORE_URL/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/promotions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OORE_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"build_id": "'"$BUILD_ID"'", "environment_id": "'"$ENVIRONMENT_ID"'", "reason": "QA signed off"}'
```

The build is promoted from its newest release in the target's store that is
rolling out, paused or complete. A halted or failed release cannot be
promoted. On the App Store, that is a TestFlight release Oore uploaded; a
release on the App Store itself is the end of the path.

If App Store Connect cannot take the build, the promotion fails and the
dialog shows why. See [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).

## 3. Approve a promotion

When the target track requires approval, the promotion waits under
**Waiting for approval** on the **Releases** tab, the track shows **Approve**, and nothing changes in the store. Each waiting
promotion says who can approve it. One of them selects **Approve** to make the
store change, or **Reject** to drop it. The approval is the release's
approval, so the new release does not wait again.

### Choose who approves

By default any app maintainer approves. To narrow or widen that, edit the
track on the **Stores** tab and, with **Require approval** on, set:

- **Who can approve**: Maintainers, Developers and maintainers, or Only named
  approvers.
- **Named approvers**: app members who are developers or maintainers. A
  named developer can approve even when developers as a whole cannot.

Someone may approve when their role is allowed, or when they are named. With
only named approvers, other maintainers cannot approve or reject; they get
`403 permission_denied`. Instance owners and admins can always approve.
Approvals are interactive: an API token cannot approve or reject a promotion,
whatever its role, and gets `403 permission_denied`. Maintainers can still
edit the track, including its approvers, and the audit log records each
change.

From the API, set `approvers` when you create or update the environment
(the track). It
replaces the whole set; leaving it out, or sending `null`, keeps the current
set, and `{}` goes back to any maintainer (so does `"role": "maintainer"` with
nobody named). Only app members who are developers or maintainers can be
named (otherwise `400 invalid_input`), at most 20.

```bash
curl -X PATCH "$OORE_URL/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/environments/$ENVIRONMENT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OORE_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "approvers": { "role": "maintainer", "user_ids": ["'"$QA_LEAD_ID"'"] } }'
```

Someone removed from the app, or changed to the viewer role, stops being
an approver. If no named approvers are left and no role is set, any
maintainer approves again.

The person who asked for a promotion can approve it when they are an
approver. The `promotion_approved` audit entry records `self_approval`,
`decided_as` (`maintainer`, `approver_role`, `named_approver` or
`instance_admin`) and the track's approvers at that moment.

Approval applies to promotions only. A maintainer who records a release
directly with [Create release](/openapi/operations/create_release)
(`POST /v1/releases`) on a track's store destination does not go through
the track's approval.

Deleting a track rejects its promotions that are waiting for approval,
with the reason `environment deleted` in the audit log.

## Verify the result

- On the **Releases** tab, the track shows the promoted version and its
  rollout.
- **Recent promotions** lists the promotion with who approved it. A failed
  promotion shows its error there.
- Play Console shows the version code on the target track. For the App
  Store, App Store Connect shows the build in the TestFlight group, or
  attached to the App Store version.
- **Versions** on the same tab lists the version with every store it went
  to. Each release opens its own page with its history and controls.
- The audit log has `promotion_requested`, `promotion_approved` and
  `promotion_completed` entries, and a `release_created` entry for the new
  release.

## Troubleshooting

### **Promote** is missing on a track

Promotion moves a build toward tracks listed after it, in the same
store. **Promote** shows only when the track has a release that is
rolling out, paused, or complete, and a later track in the same store
can take it. Developers see it only toward a track that requires
approval. A track shows one action at a time: a waiting approval, a halt or
a resume comes before **Promote**.

### The dialog says the build already has a release there

A build cannot be promoted into a track where it already has a
release, unless that release failed.

### The dialog says a promotion is already waiting for approval

Someone already asked to promote this build there. One of the track's
approvers approves or rejects it under **Waiting for approval**.

### Approve says only certain people can approve

The track names its approvers. The message and the waiting promotion
say who they are. Ask one of them, or have a maintainer change the
track's approvers.

### An App Store promotion fails

The promotion fails with `409` and one of these codes. Nothing changes in App
Store Connect:

| Code                          | Meaning                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no_source_release`           | The build has no TestFlight release that testers have, or Oore did not upload it.                                                        |
| `build_expired`               | The build expired in TestFlight (after 90 days). Upload a new build.                                                                     |
| `no_editable_version`         | The app has no App Store version Apple lets you edit. Create the version in App Store Connect.                                           |
| `version_mismatch`            | The editable version has another version string, such as 1.3.0 for a 1.2.0 build. Oore never renames it; change it in App Store Connect. |
| `version_not_editable`        | The version for this version string is in review or live, so no other build can be attached.                                             |
| `version_held_by_other_build` | Another build's release is in review or releasing on this version. Wait until it finishes or fails.                                      |
| `testflight_group_not_found`  | App Store Connect has no TestFlight group with the track's group name.                                                                   |

Other App Store Connect errors fail the promotion with `502 store_rejected`.
A step may already have happened, such as attaching the build. The calls are
safe to repeat, so promote again once the cause is fixed.

### A promotion shows "interrupted by daemon restart"

The daemon stopped during the store call. Check Play Console or App Store
Connect before you promote again, because the change may have reached the
store.

### The release stays **In review**

Apple is reviewing the build for an external TestFlight group, or the App
Store version for release. Follow the review in App Store Connect.

## Limits

- A build is promoted within one store. App Store releases are promoted from
  TestFlight only; an App Store version is not promoted further.
- A promotion into the App Store never creates or renames an App Store
  version. Uploads that publish straight to the App Store do.
- Per-track notification channels, QA groups and secrets are not
  configurable yet.
